clue.text: Blank husband overwhelmed by ingenuity and energy

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is swamped and engulfed, so it ends up surrounded by the other piece

parts.note: wit is cleverness or ingenuity
H is the standard abbreviation for husband
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dull, empty husband is outshone by a partner full of wit and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside WIT to make WHIT, then E is added to finish WHITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A white page or space is one left empty, with nothing written on it, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Wife, say, adopting twin daughters in marriage

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in and give a home, so one piece takes others inside itself

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
e.g. means 'for example', which is what 'say' means here
D is daughter, and twins make two of them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wife takes in twin daughters as part of the marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the usual crossword signal for 'for example', abbreviated e.g.; 'in' looks like a connector but is used as letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding is the ceremony of marriage, and the words are commonly used as synonyms for being wed.

clue.text: Sensitivity shown by angry Blairite about Republican head

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the rearranged letters go round another one
an angry person is worked up and stirred, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: a supporter of Tony Blair, used for its letters
R is the abbreviation for Republican
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A furious Blair supporter rants about a Republican leader, showing touchiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a leader beside Republican, but it is the geographical sense, a headland. NESS turns up in many British place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritableness is a tendency to take offence or react quickly, a touchy oversensitivity to small provocations.

clue.text: Participate in nothing after internet breaks

indicators.note: 'after' means coming later, so the piece named first in the clue is placed second
something that breaks falls to pieces, and the pieces can be put back in a new order

parts.note: the word used for its letters
O looks like zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: When the internet goes down, you can take part in nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the O at the end of the jumbled letters. 'Breaks' reads like an outage, but it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter into a discussion or agreement is to join it and take part, a phrasal verb meaning to participate.

clue.text: Female, insulated, became weak

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
pipes are lagged when wrapped in insulating material

explanation.surface: A woman, wrapped up against the cold, still lost her strength.
explanation.walkthrough: Lagging is the British word for the insulation wrapped round pipes and boilers.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or lose energy, so something that flagged grew feeble over time.

clue.text: Fishing tackle's fine line brought up fish

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
L is the abbreviation for line

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up lifts it bottom to top, so it reads the other way

parts.note: the dory, or John Dory, is a sea fish

explanation.surface: An angler's gear includes a thin line that hauls up a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine line' reads as fishing line, but each word gives one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly rod is a light, flexible rod used for fly fishing, so it is a piece of angling equipment.

clue.text: Fool starts off Alexei Sayle Show

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A clown kicks off the British comedian's television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alexei Sayle Show was a British comedy series of the 1990s; only its initials matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a silly or stupid person, an everyday insult meaning an idiot or dolt.

clue.text: Large mission evolves around European supreme commander

indicators.note: 'around' means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap round another
whatever evolves develops into a new form, so these letters change their order

parts.note: the two words used for their letters
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A big military operation develops around a European top commander.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a campaign growing, but 'Large mission' is just the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A generalissimo is the officer in overall charge of a nation's armed forces, ranking above all other generals.

clue.text: Miserable, as is this clue

definitions.meaning: first meaning: low in spirits, depressed
second meaning: the clue's place in the grid, read top to bottom

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition refers to the clue itself: it sits in the column of vertical entries.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means being sad and dejected, and the clue is numbered among the vertical entries of the grid.

clue.text: Girl temporarily in Oz crashed hotrod back in Sydney

indicators.note: a crashed car is wrecked and mangled, so these letters come out in a new order

parts.note: a souped-up car, used for its letters

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the city name

explanation.surface: A young woman visiting Australia wrecked a souped-up car back in Sydney.
explanation.walkthrough: Oz is slang for Australia, which Sydney supports, but here it is the Land of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy Gale is the heroine of The Wizard of Oz, who visits that land briefly before going home to Kansas.

clue.text: Tendon function beginning to weaken

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tendon's job starts to weaken, as after an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' reads as what the tendon does, but it is the mathematical function.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew is the tough fibrous tissue joining muscle to bone, which is exactly what a tendon is.

clue.text: Turbocharger components adapted on lorries etc

indicators.note: something adapted has been modified and altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the words used for their letters

explanation.surface: Parts for turbochargers have been modified to fit trucks and similar vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: A lorry is the British word for a truck; 'etc' supplies letters too.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercooler cools the compressed air from a turbocharger before it enters the engine, so it is part of the system.

clue.text: Stops announcement of holiday cancellation?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ceases or discontinues doing something
second meaning: a notice that time away from work is called off

explanation.walkthrough: Leave is time off work, so a notice that all leave is cancelled could be read as this phrase; the question mark flags the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave off is an idiom meaning to cease, and read literally the phrase declares that holiday leave is cancelled.

clue.text: Taunting grown-up about his banal logic, essentially

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a grown-up child is big

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the central letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone mocks an adult for his tedious, simplistic reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it signals turning round; 'grown-up' must be read as an adjective meaning large.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibing is jeering or making scornful remarks, which is the same as mocking someone with taunts.

clue.text: District inside NYC border welcomes patrols every so often

indicators.note: to welcome guests is to take them in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a hem is the edge or border of cloth

indicators.note: taking something only now and then means skipping, so alternate letters are kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: An area of New York near its edge gets occasional police patrols.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside NYC' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay; 'border' looks geographical but is the sewing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlem is a well-known neighbourhood in northern Manhattan, one of New York City's districts.

clue.text: Executive chap, one getting more mature

parts.note: a chap is a man
one who ages is an ager

explanation.surface: A business executive, a man who is getting older.
explanation.walkthrough: AGER is a crossword favourite: a thing or person that ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An executive is a person with authority to run part of an organisation, which is what a manager does.

clue.text: Inventor is getting stuck into English academic

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: something stuck into another is pushed inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
taken as written

explanation.surface: An inventor is tucking into work with an English professor.
explanation.walkthrough: Don is the British word for a college lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge, and a crossword staple for 'academic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American who devised the phonograph and a practical light bulb, a famous example of the type.

clue.text: Child on back by you

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a child riding piggyback is an extra rider on the carrier
second meaning: the grammatical category of the pronoun addressing the listener

explanation.surface: A youngster rides piggyback, carried by you.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is playful: a child carried on someone's back adds one more individual to the load.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the pronoun used for the person spoken to belongs to this category, between first and third.

clue.text: Seal off earth's mantle

parts.note: to cap off something is to seal its top
E is the abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: Geology: sealing off the layer beneath the Earth's crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth's mantle' looks like the geological layer, but the mantle here is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantle is a loose sleeveless cloak, and a cape is the same kind of outer garment hanging from the shoulders.

clue.text: First-class male spy

parts.note: A is a first-class grade
a gent is a gentleman

explanation.surface: A top-notch man working in espionage.
explanation.walkthrough: A for first-class comes from grades and the old A1 rating.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret agent is someone employed to gather intelligence covertly, the standard meaning of a spy.

clue.text: Digital item ultimately put to use

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A piece of digital technology finally gets put to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests computers, but it means relating to digits, which include toes as well as fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Toes are the digits of the foot, so one is literally an item among the body's digits.

clue.text: Society medical officer confronting monarch's unhealthy habit?

indicators.note: to confront is to stand face to face in front of, so the earlier piece goes before the next

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society
MO is the abbreviation for medical officer
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A society doctor confronts the king about his bad health habit.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, medical officer, is a military doctor's title; the question mark warns that the definition is one example of an unhealthy habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoking tobacco is the classic example of a damaging habit; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Oriental festival before first of November

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the month

explanation.surface: An Asian celebration held before the start of November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Festival' tempts a search for an Asian holiday, but it is a Christian spring one.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental describes things from Asia, in the east of the world, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: John initially rallies following loud defeat

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
a john and a loo are both slang for a toilet

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: John recovers at first after a resounding loss.
explanation.walkthrough: John looks like a person's name, but it is the toilet; loo is the British word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor an opponent is to knock them down or beat them, so the verb is a synonym for defeat.
